name: Kaunerberg
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny highland balcony above the Kaunertal entrance featuring the historic irrigation channel, Gallruth Tunnel, and alpine orchards.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kaunerberg extends across an altitude of 1,297 metres on a sun-drenched mountain shelf in the Tyrolean Oberland within the district of Landeck. Comprising roughly 468 residents, the municipality is organized as an idyllic scattered settlement featuring historic hamlets such as Unterfalpetan, Oberfalpetan, Martinsbach, and Maierhof. Perched high above the Inn Valley and the entrance to the Kaunertal, Kaunerberg affords magnificent panoramic vistas toward the Samnaun Alps and the Ötztal Alps. A remarkable geographical feature is its dry inner-alpine microclimate with only about 600 millimetres of annual rainfall. Combined with intense solar radiation, this unique climate fosters North Tyrol's highest contiguous fruit-growing region, where apples, pears, and plums flourish at over 1,300 metres above sea level. As part of the Nature Park Kaunergrat, the village is an oasis of alpine tranquility.

History

The settlement of these sunlit slopes began during the High Middle Ages through coordinated land clearing. In 1288, the land registry of Count Meinhard II of Tyrol first recorded the mountain farmsteads alongside the historic Maierhof manor. Historically governed under the jurisdiction of Laudeck, Kaunerberg formed an economic cooperative with Kauns and Faggen. Due to extreme seasonal dryness, survival depended on sophisticated irrigation channels known as Waale. Between 1947 and 1954, supported by the American Marshall Plan, local engineers accomplished a masterpiece of alpine engineering: the Kaunerberg Slope Canal. Its centrepiece is the 996-metre Gallruth Tunnel, which channels glacial meltwater from the Gallruth Glacier through solid rock. Ecclesiastically linked to Kauns, the community cherishes local heritage chapels including the 1866 Saint Martin's Chapel in Obwals and the octagonal Maierhof Chapel dating to 1677.

Getting There

Drivers travel via the Inntal Autobahn A12 through the Landeck Tunnel onto the B180 Reschenstraße as far as Prutz. From there, take the L63 Kaunertalstraße to Faggen, where the L250 Kaunerbergstraße ascends in panoramic switchbacks onto the sunny terrace. Alternatively, motorists can arrive via the L17 Piller Landesstraße connecting with the Pitztal. Rail travellers take long-distance trains to the Landeck-Zams railway station on the Arlberg rail line. Frequent VVT buses depart the station for Prutz, offering convenient connections to regional bus route 231 serving Kauns and Kaunerberg. In summer, seasonal nature park shuttles connect the hamlets directly to the Nature Park House atop Piller Sattel.

Tips

One of Tyrol's most thrilling walking routes is the Kaunerberg Waterway along the historical irrigation canal. Traversing the 996-metre Gallruth Tunnel requires a flashlight and sturdy boots, rewarding adventurous walkers with an unforgettable underground journey through cool rock. For alpine dining, the Falkaunsalm at 1,963 metres and the Gallruthalm offer artisanal mountain cheese on sun-drenched panoramic terraces. Nearby on the Piller Sattel mountain pass, the Nature Park House Kaunergrat showcases the interactive '3000 Meters Vertical' exhibition and the dramatic Gacher Blick viewing platform, suspended 800 metres above the sheer cliffs of the Inn Valley. A tranquil loop through the neighbouring Piller Moor boardwalk nature trail provides an ideal family excursion.
